observation: In audit mode the architect must record a verdict per capability (real / decorative / missing / silently-failing) but the capability status enum only expresses build progress, so the verdict has to be smuggled into the rationale prose. The manifest cannot then be queried for 'show me every decorative screen'.
proposedChange: Add an optional capability field such as auditVerdict with an enum of live, partial, decorative, missing, silently-failing, and teach `report` and `coverage` to summarise by it.

observation: The single most damaging pattern found in this codebase was a catch block whose body is identical to the try block, so every failure reports success. It defeats RLS observability, hides unapplied migrations and makes a decorative screen indistinguishable from a working one. It is not named in capability-catalog.md or verification.md.
proposedChange: Add 'catch-and-succeed' to the anti-pattern list in capability-catalog.md, and add a grep-based check to verification.md: a catch block that calls the same success setter as its try block is a defect.

observation: Several screens substitute demo data when a query returns ZERO ROWS rather than when it errors. This is more dangerous than an error fallback because it fires in normal operation on a quiet month - a VAT screen showed invented tax totals this way. The discovery reference warns about placeholder data but not about this specific trigger.
proposedChange: In discovery.md and verification.md, state explicitly that a zero-row result must render an empty state and never substitute sample data, and call out financial and compliance screens as absolute.

observation: Supabase Edge Functions default to verify_jwt=true, which developers read as 'authenticated', but the check is satisfied by the project's public publishable/anon key that ships in every browser bundle. Two service-role functions here relied on it and had no role check of their own. stack-adapters.md does not warn about this.
proposedChange: Add to the Supabase section of stack-adapters.md: verify_jwt is not authorization; every service-role Edge Function must independently call auth.getUser on the bearer token and check the role, and Access-Control-Allow-Origin should not be '*' on a privileged function.

observation: The most consequential question in this audit - which migrations are applied to the live project - was unanswerable because the Supabase MCP server was unauthenticated in a non-interactive session. Roughly a third of the security findings had to be stated conditionally.
proposedChange: Have the audit agent check for live-database reachability at the START of the pass and, when it is missing, say so in the first paragraph of the report and list precisely which findings are conditional on it, rather than discovering the limitation midway.
